review.central_scientific_object: Serving-induced selective trajectory logging in persistent self-evolution: a search system generates a shared candidate pool T_K, an acting selector a(T_K) chooses the served trajectory, and a learning projection g(T_K) determines what an external persistent skill updater observes. The scientific object is the coupling between a and g, specifically the default winner-only coupling g_win = a, which creates a missing-not-at-random observation process for the updater. This is a specialized instance of selective labels and performative prediction, not a new general phenomenon.
claims_to_delete: Any claim that failures are useful for skill evolution (reduced by Rethinking Self-Evolving Agent Skills, arXiv:2608.02636)
Any claim of first use of sibling rollouts, success/failure contrast, or first-divergence extraction (reduced by SkillCAT, Search-E1, SGCD, OVCSD, SKILL-KD)
Any claim that outcome filtering discards useful branch structure (reduced by TopoCurate, arXiv:2603.01714)
Any claim that more test-time compute universally harms learning (falsified by TSR, Expert Iteration, AlphaZero-style distillation)
Any claim of discovering selective labels, performative prediction, or decision-dependent data (mature conceptual reductions)
The mutual-information quantity D_g = I(Z; g(T_K) | x, S_t) as a measured mechanism (decorative outside controlled suite; data-processing inequality is vacuous for fixed LLM updater)
The i.i.d. Bernoulli curve and p*(K) as empirical results (reference model only; correlated rollouts destroy the peak location)
The continuous-verifier layer-cake identity as a substantive extension (standard representation; adds no empirical content unless threshold policy is used)
The Gamma-times-delta factorization as a non-tautological result (exact only under gated-projection construction; scientific content is entirely in whether delta_z is positive and predictable)

Any claim that the old R3 runner implements the R4 same-pool intervention (it uses an independent K=1 shadow, not a same-pool precommitted rollout-0, and forbids nonselected failures from updater input)
Any claim that CADP is necessary if Rejected-Witness suffices (simpler method dominance rule)
Any longitudinal causal claim from the one-step cloned-state design (one-step identifies projection effect, not multi-round path-dependent evolution)
review.decisive_intervention: The cloned-state exact-same-pool projection-null experiment (F2). Take one fixed pre-update skill state S, one task batch, one exact K-pool T_K with frozen hashes, one acting winner served by a deterministic selector, one fixed updater, one update seed. Clone S into arms that differ only in g(T_K): winner-only versus precommitted rejected-witness (frozen rule, chosen before outcomes) versus contrast packet. Then freeze all skills and evaluate on a common held-out probe with K=1, same backbone, temperature, and tool harness. The scientific unit is the cloned learned-skill state, not individual rollouts. If changing g(T_K) produces no directional difference in future frozen skill J(U(S,g(T_K))) in the preregistered direction—especially in mixed rescue pools with positive estimated delta—the central mechanism is dead. This single experiment isolates the entire causal claim: that the learning projection, not the acting projection or compute amount, drives persistent skill quality.
review.explicit_stop_condition: STOP if the cloned-state exact-same-pool projection-null experiment (F2) shows no directional effect of changing the learning projection on future frozen skill, under the preregistered direction and on a qualified substrate. Specifically: if winner-only versus Rejected-Witness on mixed rescue pools with positive estimated delta_z produces no significant difference in J(U(S,g(T_K))) across independent cloned skill states, the central mechanism is dead. Additional STOP triggers: (1) if a source-faithful SkillCAT-style contrast baseline reproduces the full effect without the serving-selection causal chain, reducing R17 to an application; (2) if the prospective Gamma-times-delta law fails sign or rank prediction on held-out cells; (3) if duplicated-winner token-matched controls match the Rejected-Witness effect, attributing the result to updater context budget rather than diagnostic evidence.
review.mechanism_derived_method: The Rejected-Witness projection: in mixed rescue pools, feed the updater one precommitted, frozen-rule nonserved failure witness from the same K-pool instead of the served winner. This is the simplest method that follows naturally from the mechanism. It requires no extra actor rollouts, no contrast packet construction, and no additional updater tokens beyond a single trajectory. CADP (contrastive diagnostic projection) should be demoted to an optional variant unless it beats Rejected-Witness under matched token budgets. If Rejected-Witness matches CADP, the paper retains the rollout-recycling claim but drops any need for counterfactual branch generation or contrastive packets. The method is not novel as a skill-editing technique (SkillCAT collision); its only role is to test whether preserving censored failure evidence rescues persistent learning.
review.recommendation: REVISE_AND_NARROW with conditional STOP. Reframe the paper as a mechanism-level causal study of serving-induced selective trajectory logging in persistent self-evolution. The exact rescue-censoring identity is a definitional tool, not a theorem. Demote CADP to a simple Rejected-Witness baseline unless contrast beats it under matched budgets. Add SkillCAT and TopoCurate as mandatory baselines, with SkillCAT as the strongest direct reduction. Freeze a mutually exclusive failure-family partition and the rejected-witness rule before outcomes. Replace the old R3 runner with a new same-pool projection runner. Do not present the i.i.d. curve, MI bound, or layer-cake identity as empirical results. The decisive F2 cloned-state projection-null experiment must pass before any longitudinal or prospective claims. If SkillCAT-style contrast explains the full effect without the serving-selection causal chain, reduce to an application or stop. Do not execute any experiment until the R4 contract is frozen and the runner is replaced.
review.single_causal_chain: Best-of-K winner selection improves current acting reward A_K relative to A_1. Under winner-only learning projection g_win = a, the updater observes only the served winner. On the rescue-censoring event M = {precommitted rollout fails, at least one other rollout succeeds}, the updater loses visibility of a failure trajectory that a precommitted branch would have shown. If that censored failure has positive reusable diagnostic value delta > 0 for the updater, then the updated skill S_{t+1} is weaker under winner-only than under a projection that preserves the failure witness, as measured by frozen K=1 held-out evaluation J(S_{t+1}). The causal chain is: winner selection -> censoring of failure evidence on event M -> weaker persistent skill -> lower future frozen performance. Each link requires independent verification; the chain is not established by the identity alone.
review.single_sentence_verdict: R17 has a narrow but potentially real mechanism-level novelty—serving-time winner selection endogenously censoring diagnostic failures from an external persistent updater, with an exact rescue-censoring identity and a same-pool projection intervention—but it is currently buried under method components already published by SkillCAT and TopoCurate, the central causal claim is only testable through a single decisive cloned-state projection-null experiment that has not been run, and the paper must survive a source-faithful SkillCAT-style contrast baseline before any novelty claim is defensible.
review.strongest_theoretical_prediction: The independence-free rescue-censoring identity A_K - A_1 = Pr(Y_1=0, max_i Y_i=1) = Gamma_K(Q) is a definitional tool, not a theorem. The strongest falsifiable theoretical prediction is the prospective Gamma-times-delta law: for a pre-outcome frozen, mutually exclusive failure-family partition Z, the expected frozen-skill deficit from winner-only versus a gated alternative projection equals sum over z of Pr(M, Z=z) times delta_z, where delta_z is estimated from cloned-state one-step interventions. This prediction is falsifiable because it requires sign accuracy, rank correlation, and calibration on held-out task cells that were never used to estimate p_z or delta_z. If the prospective law fails on unseen cells, the mechanism claim is dead regardless of any post-hoc fit.
